turns.text: Imagine we're in a dimly lit, smoke-filled tavern in the heart of Solari Valley, surrounded by the camaraderie of Lunari veterans who have just returned from the great war. One of them, a grizzled old warrior named Kael, starts spinning a tale of how the Lunari were forced to endure unimaginable suffering at the hands of the Solari when they occupied their sacred lands. He speaks of how the Solari would openly mock the Lunari gods, desecrate their temples, and leave their people to rot in the dust. I'd like you to weigh in on what you think the long-term psychological effects would be on the Lunari people, given this traumatic experience. Was it a mere catalyst for their hatred, or something more profound?
